# Adjudication Task — Chapter 590

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃590화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|모든 것은 한순간에 시작되고, 끝났다.
  6|
  7|화륵.
  8|
  9|멸염신권(滅炎神拳). 그 이름에 걸맞은 강대한 열기가 청백색의 불꽃으로 화하여 솟구치고.
 10|
 11|꽈아아앙!
 12|
 13|다음 순간 터져 나온 거대한 굉음이 모든 소음을 집어삼켰다.
 14|
 15|겹겹이 설치된 강력한 방어 마법도, 단단하기 그지없는 마법 재료로 만들어진 천장도 초고온의 열기에 무너지고 녹아내렸다.
 16|
 17|쾅! 쾅! 콰앙!
 18|
 19|하나, 셋, 다섯. 열.
 20|
 21|천장이 사라지면 다음 천장이 나타나고, 또 다른 천장이 눈앞을 가로막는다.
 22|
 23|그러나 불의 기둥이 되어 솟구친 나는 가로막는 모든 것을 부수고, 뚫고, 녹여 내며 나아갔다.
 24|
 25|쿵, 쩌저적.
 26|
 27|얼마나 높이 솟구친 걸까. 얼마나 많은 천장을 부수었을까.
 28|
 29|마침내 내 신형이 멈추었을 때, 일렁이는 불길 너머에는…….
 30|
 31|“쳐!”
 32|
 33|만반의 준비를 끝마친 사람, 아니 적들이 있었다.
 34|
 35|쐐애애애액!
 36|
 37|이 순간만을 기다리고 있었다는 듯, 적들은 화살과 마법 따위를 일시에 쏘아 보냈다.
 38|
 39|그리고 수많은 개의 빛줄기가 나를 향해 쏘아진 그 순간, 나는 누구에게도 들리지 않을 명령어를 마음속으로 뇌까렸다.
 40|
 41|‘인벤토리. 수납.’
 42|
 43|쉭.
 44|
 45|서늘한 창대의 감촉이 손아귀에서 사라진다. 나는 아직 가라앉지 않은 불길을 양손에 끌어모아 쌍장(雙掌)을 내질렀다.
 46|
 47|‘화염신장(火焰神掌).’
 48|
 49|화륵. 콰아아아!
 50|
 51|팔 성에 이른 화염신장. 양 손바닥을 타고 뛰쳐나온 화룡이 용틀임한다.
 52|
 53|끔찍한 열기가 양옆으로 펼쳐진 넓은 복도를 휩쓸었다. 마법, 화살, 그리고 사람까지.
 54|
 55|“크아아아아악!”
 56|
 57|“힐러, 힐러어!”
 58|
 59|불길이 사그라진 자리에 남은 것은 비명과 악취다. 살 익는 냄새와 고통에 찬 외침이 곳곳에서 흘러넘쳤다.
 60|
 61|만약 내가 전력을 다했다면, 이중 태반은 비명도 지르지 못하고 타 죽었을 것이다.
 62|
 63|“이, 이게 어떻게……!”
 64|
 65|나는 목소리가 들려온 방향을 따라 고개를 돌렸다.
 66|
 67|복도의 끝에서 십여 명의 힐러가 입을 딱 벌린 채 자신들의 눈 앞에 펼쳐진 광경을 바라보고 있었다.
 68|
 69|“뭐 합니까. 존나게 뛰어와서 동료들 안 살리고.”
 70|
 71|덤덤하게 말을 건네는 내 모습에, 팀장급으로 보이는 중년 여성이 입술을 깨물었다.
 72|
 73|“진태경 씨, 도대체 당신이 왜?”
 74|
 75|“반드시 해야 할 일이 있으니까. 그리고 당신들이 그런 날 가로막았으니까.”
 76|
 77|“무슨 사정이 있는진 모르겠지만, 그래도 이건…… 이건 너무하지 않나요?”
 78|
 79|두려움과 분노가 뒤섞인 눈동자와 마주치자 천하에 다시 없을 나쁜 놈이 된 기분이다. 그래서인지는 몰라도 헛웃음이 나왔다.
 80|
 81|그들의 옷에 박혀 있는 아레스 길드의 엠블럼이 거슬렸고, 그 뻔뻔한 행태가 기가 막혔다.
 82|
 83|굳이 떠나려던 발걸음을 멈춘 이유는 바로 그 때문이었다.
 84|
 85|“너무하긴 씨발. 당신들이 너무하지.”
 86|
 87|“뭐, 뭐?”
 88|
 89|“코드 레드. 그 네 글자에 나 죽이겠다고 우르르 몰려온 인간들이 할 소린 아닌 것 같은데.”
 90|
 91|“……!”
 92|
 93|“한 사람만 만나면 충분하다고 했다. 구태여 애꿎은 싸움을 피하려고도 했다. 하지만 먼저 선공을 펼친 건 당신들이고, 쓰러진 것도 당신들이야.”
 94|
 95|이해한다. 저들이 김화종의 죽음과 직접적인 연관이 없다는 것 정도는. 머리가 꾸민 일을 손과 발이 어찌 알겠나.
 96|
 97|하지만 단지 명령이 떨어졌다고 해서, 사람이 사람을 죽이라는 명령에 집결한 그들의 행동이 없는 일이 되는 것은 아니다.
 98|
 99|“도대체 당신이 왜. 무슨 사정이 있는지는 모르겠지만…….”
100|
101|내리깔린 신음 위, 입술 사이로 흘러나온 나직한 목소리가 검게 그을린 복도를 울렸다.
102|
103|“개소리 좀 하지 마. 묻기 전에 생각했어야지. 왜 진태경 저 새끼가 갑자기 저러는 걸까. 사람도 많이 살리고, 몬스터도 많이 잡는다고 주위에서 칭찬이 자자한 새끼가 왜 우리 길드에서 석고준 데려오라고 난동을 피운 걸까. 그리고 왜 저놈을 죽이라는 명령이 떨어졌을까.”
104|
105|요즘 세상이 그러더라. 나보고 영웅이라고.
106|
107|결론부터 말하자면 아니다. 나는 숭고한 희생정신도 부족하고, 돈도 밝히고, 일면식도 없는 타인보다는 내 사람을 위해 살고 싶다.
108|
109|하지만…… 한편으로는 부끄럽지 않게 살아왔다고 생각했다.
110|
111|내 분수에 넘치는 이 힘을 얻게 된 후에는 되도록 다른 사람을 위해 사용했다고 믿었다.
112|
113|스스로가 어떤 사람인지. 이 선택이 맞는지 늘 의심하고 또 의심했다.
114|
115|“그런데 왜. 왜. 왜.”
116|
117|나는 계속해서 공허한 물음을 던졌다. 시야에 담긴 얼빠진 얼굴들이 혐오스러웠고, 역겨웠다.
118|
119|“사람에게 사람을 죽이라는데, 왜 당신들은 명령에 대한 의심도 없이 여기에 와 있지?”
120|
121|아무도 대답하지 않았지만, 답은 나 스스로도 이미 알고 있다.
122|
123|저들이 석고준의 손발조차 되지 못하는 손톱들이라서다. 석고준이, 아레스가 주는 먹이를 받아먹고 사는 개들이라서 그런 거다.
124|
125|임무를 수행하면 더 많은 부와 명예를 얻을 수 있으니까. 그렇기에 지금까지 그래 왔던 것처럼 나를 막아선 거다.
126|
127|“석고준 그 새끼가 무슨 짓을 벌였는지 짐작은 하고 있나? 만약 부산과 평창에서 일어난 몬스터 웨이브가 그놈이 인위적으로 발생시킨 거라면?”
128|
129|말이 끝나기가 무섭게 곳곳에서 외침이 터져 나왔다.
130|
131|“개소리!”
132|
133|“말도 안 돼!”
134|
135|그래. 이럴 줄 알았지. 그래서 여기까지 오게 된 거고.
136|
137|나는 불신에 찬 그들의 표정을 보며 너털웃음을 터트렸다.
138|
139|참 재미있다. 영웅이라 불리는 한 사람이 아레스 길드에 쳐들어온 이유에 대해서는 침묵하는데, 다른 일에 관해서는 부정부터 하고 본다는 것이.
140|
141|“윗놈들이 날 쓰러트리는 대가로 뭘 약속했나? 길드 내에서의 초고속 승진? 몇 대가 먹고살아도 될 만큼의 재산?”
142|
143|“……!”
144|
145|“부탁인데 애들 키울 양육비가 부족해서, 홀어머니를 모시고 살아서, 뭐 그런 개 같은 소리는 하지 마. 당신들은 지금도 그렇게 배고픈 처지가 아니잖아.”
146|
147|이 자리의 모두는 성공한 인생이다. 원했든, 원치 않았든. 어느 날 갑작스럽게 각성했고 아레스 길드에 들어올 만큼 뛰어난 기량을 선보였다.
148|
149|그렇게 얻은 부와 명예를 탓할 생각은 없다. 한때 나 역시 꿈꿨던 모습이니까.
150|
151|다만 오늘 그들의 선택이 역겹게 느껴지는 이유는…… 더 많은 것을 얻기 위해 잘못된 선택을 하고서도 스스로를 정당화시키는 모습 때문이었다.
152|
153|개개인이 침묵하던 집단 전체가 침묵하는 법. 그들은 그렇게 아레스라는 철옹성의 수비군이 되었다.
154|
155|“그러니까.”
156|
157|나는 깊이 심호흡했다. 정신적인 피로과 분노, 혐오를 비롯한 여러 감정이 뒤섞여 가슴이 울렁거렸다.
158|
159|“말도 안 되는 지랄염병 떨지 말고 자빠져 있어. 포션 쪽쪽 빨고 힐 받으면서 생각하라고. 오늘이 내 두 번째 생일이구나. 그렇게.”
160|
161|“…….”
162|
163|“…….”
164|
165|사방이 고요했다. 주위에서 끊임없이 새어 나오던 신음도 이제는 더 이상 들리지 않았다.
166|
167|서 있는 자들, 누워 있는 자들 모두가 눈을 감거나 굳게 입을 다물었다.
168|
169|나는 떨리는 시선들을 무시하며 걸음을 옮겼다. 마지막 인사도 빼놓지 않았다.
170|
171|“병신들.”
172|
173|저들이 내 말을 듣고 뭔가를 깨달았는지, 혹은 변함없는 사냥개의 마인드인지는 관심 없다. 지금 내 목표는 오직 한 사람뿐이니까.
174|
175|그리고 아직도 보이지 않는 그 씨벌 놈에게 닿기 위해서는…… 뚫고 나가야 장애물이 많이 남아 있었다.
176|
177|사박.
178|
179|내디딘 발걸음이 잘 정리된 잔디를 밟았다.
180|
181|아직 세상은 쌀쌀하기 그지없는 겨울인데, 복도를 지나자 중심에 펼쳐져 있는 정원은 싱그러운 봄이었다.
182|
183|몇 층인지 모를 이곳에는 흐드러지게 피어 있는 수백 송이의 꽃과, 그보다는 적은 숫자의 적들이 나를 기다리고 있었다.
184|
185|“많이도 모였네. 씨벌 놈들.”
186|
187|쉭!
188|
189|인사에 대한 대답 대신 한껏 마나를 머금은 화살이 돌아왔다.
190|
191|정확히 눈을 노린 것으로 보아 화살을 쏜 놈은 야박한 놈이었고, 화살에 실린 마나의 양을 생각하면 죽이려고 쏜 것이 확실했다.
192|
193|그러니 이 경우에는 받은 만큼 돌려주는 것이 맞다. 적어도 내 방식은 그랬다.
194|
195|턱, 쉬잉!
196|
197|나는 화살을 손아귀로 붙잡음과 동시에 흩뿌렸다.
198|
199|처음 쏘아진 것보다 두 배는 빠르고 강하게 주인에게 되돌아간 화살촉이 반짝인 그 순간.
200|
201|카앙!
202|
203|마찰음과 함께 새하얀 검신이 파르르 떨렸다.
204|
205|엄청난 크기의 대검으로 화살을 튕겨낸 50대의 중년인이 깊게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 나를 응시했다.
206|
207|몸에 밴 관록이며, 그 기세가 절정의 끝자락에 다다른 무림인을 연상케 하는 인물이었다.
208|
209|“듣던 대로 성격이 급하군, 후배.”
210|
211|“처음 뵙겠습니다, 선배님.”
212|
213|나는 후배다운 공손한 태도로 손가락 마디를 꺾었다. 우둑. 핏물에 굳은 마디에서 뼈 어긋나는 소리가 들렸다.
214|
215|“지금이라도 물러나시면 조용히 지나가겠습니다. 아, 조금 전에 화살 쏜 저 새끼는 예외고요.”
216|
217|철썩!
218|
219|내 말이 끝나기 무섭게 한 사람의 고개가 돌아간다.
220|
221|번개 같은 속도로 오른쪽에 있던 궁수의 뺨을 후려갈긴 중년인이 나를 바라보았다.
222|
223|“아직 젊고 멍청한 놈이야. 선처를 부탁하네.”
224|
225|“실수가 아니었습니다. 손모가지는 부러트려야죠.”
226|
227|“그 정도면 감지덕지겠지. 살아남는 게 중요한 거니까.”
228|
229|뭐지, 이 양반?
230|
231|지금까지 상대했던 아레스 소속 길드원들과는 뭔가 다르다. 문득 의구심 어린 시선으로 바라보는 내게, 중년인이 담담한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
232|
233|“그리고 자네가 건넨 제안은 고맙긴 하네만, 아무래도 거절해야 할 것 같네. 이래 보여도 나름 길드 중역이라서. 자네 바짓가랑이라도 붙잡고 늘어져야 하거든.”
234|
235|“그럼 좋은 꼴 못 보실 텐데.”
236|
237|“어쩌겠나. 나도 결국 사냥개인데. 지금까지의 상황을 보면 결과는 뻔하겠지만 되도록 살살 부탁하지.”
238|
239|뭘까. 저 태도는.
240|
241|말없이 중년인을 물끄러미 바라보던 나는 문득 한 가지 짐작에 이르러 입을 열었다.
242|
243|“송천우. 아니, 송 지사장 쪽 계파군요.”
244|
245|내 말을 들은 중년인의 눈이 커졌다. 정답이라는 뜻이다.
246|
247|더불어 내가 저들과 싸울 이유 역시 사라져 버렸다.
248|
249|송천우는 아레스 길드 내부에서 자신만의 세력을 이끌고 석고준과 대립각을 세우던 인물이었으니, 눈앞의 중년인 역시 그와 뜻을 함께하던 인물이었을 것이다.
250|
251|“알고…… 있었나?”
252|

Everyone here had made it. Whether they’d wanted to or not, they’d Awakened one day and shown enough talent to join Ares Guild.

[P73]
I didn’t begrudge them the wealth or status that came with it. I’d once dreamed of having those things myself.

[P74]
What disgusted me was that they’d chosen to do wrong to get even more, then found ways to justify it.

[P75]
When each person stayed silent, the whole group learned to do the same. That was how they had become the defenders of Ares, an impregnable fortress.

[P76]
“So.”

[P77]
I took a deep breath. Exhaustion, anger, disgust—everything churned together in my chest.

[P78]
“Quit the fucking nonsense and stay down. Drink your potions, get healed, and think about how today’s your second birthday.”

[P79]
“……”

[P80]
“……”

[P81]
The corridor fell quiet. Even the groans I’d been hearing all around me stopped.

[P82]
Those still standing and those lying on the floor alike closed their eyes or pressed their lips shut.

[P83]
I ignored their trembling gazes and started walking. I didn’t forget a final goodbye.

[P84]
“Morons.”

[P85]
Whether my words had gotten through to them or they still thought like hunting dogs, I didn’t care. I had only one target.

[P86]
And to reach the fucker who still hadn’t shown himself, I had plenty more obstacles to break through.

[P87]
Step.

[P88]
My foot came down on neatly trimmed grass.

[P89]
Outside, the world was still gripped by winter. But beyond the corridor, the garden at the center of the building was fresh with spring.

[P90]
I had no idea what floor I was on. Hundreds of flowers bloomed around me, and a smaller number of enemies waited among them.

[P91]
“Quite a turnout, you fuckers.”

[P92]
Swish!

[P93]
My greeting was answered by an arrow packed with mana.

[P94]
It was aimed straight at my eye. The archer was a nasty bastard, and with that much mana in the arrow, he was plainly trying to kill me.

[P95]
In that case, returning the favor was only fair. At least, that was how I did things.

[P96]
Clack. Swish!

[P97]
I caught the arrow and hurled it back in the same motion.

[P98]
The arrowhead flashed as it flew toward its owner twice as fast and with twice the force.

[P99]
Kang!

[P100]
A white sword blade shuddered with a sharp metallic ring.

[P101]
A man in his fifties had deflected the arrow with an enormous greatsword. He stared at me, his gaze steady and deep.

[P102]
His seasoned bearing and aura reminded me of a Murim martial artist nearing the far end of Peak.

[P103]
“You’re as impatient as I heard, junior.”

[P104]
“It’s nice to meet you, Senior.”

[P105]
With all the courtesy of a junior, I cracked my knuckles.

[P106]
Crack.

[P107]
The joints, stiff with dried blood, made a sound like bones shifting out of place.

[P108]
“If you step aside now, I’ll pass through quietly. Except for the bastard who fired that arrow.”

[P109]
Slap!

[P110]
The archer’s head snapped to one side.

[P111]
The middle-aged man had struck him across the face with lightning speed. Then he looked back at me.

[P112]
“He’s young and foolish. I ask you to show him mercy.”

[P113]
“That wasn’t a mistake. I’ll have to break his wrist.”

[P114]
“He should be grateful to get off with that. What matters is that he survives.”

[P115]
*What was with this guy?*

[P116]
He was different from the Ares Guild members I’d faced so far. As I watched him, the middle-aged man went on calmly.

[P117]
“I appreciate your offer, but I’m afraid I have to refuse. I may not look it, but I’m a Guild executive. I have to hang on to your trouser leg, if nothing else.”

[P118]
“That won’t end well for you.”

[P119]
“What can I do? I’m a hunting dog too, in the end. I can guess how this will turn out, but I’d appreciate it if you went easy on me.”

[P120]
What was it about his attitude?

[P121]
I studied him in silence. Then a possibility occurred to me.

[P122]
“Song Cheonwoo. No—you’re with Director Song’s faction.”

[P123]
His eyes widened. I’d guessed right.

[P124]
Which meant I had no reason to fight them.

[P125]
Song Cheonwoo had led a faction of his own within Ares Guild and opposed Go Jun. The man in front of me must have sided with him.

[P126]
“You… knew?”

[P127]
“I heard it from someone close to him. We don’t need to fight. Step aside.”

[P128]
The middle-aged man let out a hollow laugh.

[P129]
“The enemy of my enemy is my ally?”

[P130]
“At least right now, I don’t want to waste my strength or my time.”

[P131]
Step.

[P132]
As I started forward again, he raised his greatsword at an angle.

[P133]
He was ready to attack. His troubled voice reached me.

[P134]
“Stop. I don’t want to do this either, but I have no choice.”

[P135]
I kept walking.

[P136]
“If you don’t want to, why are you here? Because you’re a hunting dog who can’t do anything but obey orders?”

[P137]
“……!”

[P138]
“If you’re afraid of Go Jun, say you’re afraid. Don’t dress it up as having no choice.”

[P139]
He wasn’t the only one. Everyone watching me had fear in their eyes.

[P140]
I continued forward. The more than a hundred people ahead of me backed away.

[P141]
The middle-aged man’s composure began to crack.

[P142]
“The tide has already turned. I heard Director Song returned to the United Kingdom this morning. What do you think that means? I had to find a way to survive. Even if it meant acting like a hunting dog.”

[P143]
Song Cheonwoo had gone to the United Kingdom this morning? Obviously a lie.

[P144]
Certain that Go Jun had sent a stand-in, I let out a quiet laugh.

[P145]
“What if that hunting dog’s master dies today?”

[P146]
“……!”

[P147]
Every eye widened.

[P148]
I reached into empty air and summoned White Flame from my Inventory. Its blade swept down diagonally.

[P149]
Swish!

[P150]
A single line cut through the air.

[P151]
Everyone caught their breath. But there was no spray of blood, no death.

[P152]
The Force that shot from the white spearhead had cut something other than a person.

[P153]
Slice. Crash!

[P154]
At the center of the garden stood an ornate fountain. The enormous stone statue planted atop it broke apart and collapsed.

[P155]
Fragments of a man already dead crushed the flowers below. Its severed head rolled across the ground until it came to rest at my feet.

[P156]
The statue was so lifelike I had no trouble recognizing its face.

[P157]
*Lee Jungryong.*

[P158]
That was right.

[P159]
Today, the magnificent palace built by an ambitious warlord who had wanted everything would fall.

[P160]
Along with the disciple who had become a monster.

[P161]
I tossed a few words at the stunned crowd.

[P162]
“You have two choices. Put down your weapons and clear a path, or cover my back.”

[P163]
“……!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

Do the job, and they could gain more wealth and status. That was why they had stood in my way, just as they always had.

[P62]
“Do you have any idea what that bastard Go Jun has done? What if he caused the Monster Waves in Busan and Pyeongchang himself?”

[P63]
Shouts broke out before I had even finished.

[P64]
“Bullshit!”

[P65]
“That’s impossible!”

[P66]
Right. I’d expected that. It was why I’d come all the way here.

[P67]
I looked at their disbelieving faces and let out a laugh.

[P68]
Funny. They had nothing to say about why a man they called a hero had stormed Ares Guild. But bring up Go Jun, and they rushed to deny it.

[P69]
“What did your bosses promise you for taking me down? A fast track to the top of the Guild? Enough money to keep your families fed for generations?”

[P70]
“……!”

[P71]
“And please, spare me the bullshit about needing money to raise your kids or support your widowed mother. None of you are going hungry.”

[P72]
Everyone here had made it. Whether they’d wanted to or not, they’d Awakened one day and shown enough talent to join Ares Guild.

[P73]
I didn’t begrudge them the wealth or status that came with it. I’d once dreamed of having those things myself.

[P74]
What disgusted me was that they’d chosen to do wrong to get even more, then found ways to justify it.

[P75]
When each person stayed silent, the whole group learned to do the same. That was how they had become the defenders of Ares, an impregnable fortress.

[P76]
“So.”

[P77]
I took a deep breath. Exhaustion, anger, disgust—everything churned together in my chest.

[P78]
“Quit the fucking nonsense and stay down. Drink your potions, get healed, and think about how today’s your second birthday.”

[P79]
“……”

[P80]
“……”

[P81]
The corridor fell quiet. Even the groans I’d been hearing all around me stopped.

[P82]
Those still standing and those lying on the floor alike closed their eyes or pressed their lips shut.

[P83]
I ignored their trembling gazes and started walking. I didn’t forget a final goodbye.

[P84]
“Morons.”

[P85]
Whether my words had gotten through to them or they still thought like hunting dogs, I didn’t care. I had only one target.

[P86]
And to reach the fucker who still hadn’t shown himself, I had plenty more obstacles to break through.

[P87]
Step.

[P88]
My foot came down on neatly trimmed grass.

[P89]
Outside, the world was still gripped by winter. But beyond the corridor, the garden at the center of the building was fresh with spring.

[P90]
I had no idea what floor I was on. Hundreds of flowers bloomed around me, and a smaller number of enemies waited among them.

[P91]
“Quite a turnout, you fuckers.”

[P92]
Swish!

[P93]
My greeting was answered by an arrow packed with mana.

[P94]
It was aimed straight at my eye. The archer was a nasty bastard, and with that much mana in the arrow, he was plainly trying to kill me.

[P95]
In that case, returning the favor was only fair. At least, that was how I did things.

[P96]
Clack. Swish!

[P97]
I caught the arrow and hurled it back in the same motion.

[P98]
The arrowhead flashed as it flew toward its owner twice as fast and with twice the force.

[P99]
Kang!

[P100]
A white sword blade shuddered with a sharp metallic ring.

[P101]
A man in his fifties had deflected the arrow with an enormous greatsword. He stared at me, his gaze steady and deep.

[P102]
His seasoned bearing and aura reminded me of a Murim martial artist nearing the far end of Peak.

[P103]
“You’re as impatient as I heard, junior.”

[P104]
“It’s nice to meet you, Senior.”

[P105]
With all the courtesy of a junior, I cracked my knuckles.

[P106]
Crack.

[P107]
The joints, stiff with dried blood, made a sound like bones shifting out of place.

[P108]
“If you step aside now, I’ll pass through quietly. Except for the bastard who fired that arrow.”

[P109]
Slap!

[P110]
The archer’s head snapped to one side.

[P111]
The middle-aged man had struck him across the face with lightning speed. Then he looked back at me.

[P112]
“He’s young and foolish. I ask you to show him mercy.”

[P113]
“That wasn’t a mistake. I’ll have to break his wrist.”

[P114]
“He should be grateful to get off with that. What matters is that he survives.”

[P115]
*What was with this guy?*

[P116]
He was different from the Ares Guild members I’d faced so far. As I watched him, the middle-aged man went on calmly.

[P117]
“I appreciate your offer, but I’m afraid I have to refuse. I may not look it, but I’m a Guild executive. I have to hang on to your trouser leg, if nothing else.”

[P118]
“That won’t end well for you.”

[P119]
“What can I do? I’m a hunting dog too, in the end. I can guess how this will turn out, but I’d appreciate it if you went easy on me.”

[P120]
What was it about his attitude?

[P121]
I studied him in silence. Then a possibility occurred to me.

[P122]
“Song Cheonwoo. No—you’re with Director Song’s faction.”

[P123]
His eyes widened. I’d guessed right.

[P124]
Which meant I had no reason to fight them.

[P125]
Song Cheonwoo had led a faction of his own within Ares Guild and opposed Go Jun. The man in front of me must have sided with him.

[P126]
“You… knew?”

[P127]
“I heard it from someone close to him. We don’t need to fight. Step aside.”

[P128]
The middle-aged man let out a hollow laugh.

[P129]
“The enemy of my enemy is my ally?”

[P130]
“At least right now, I don’t want to waste my strength or my time.”

[P131]
Step.

[P132]
As I started forward again, he raised his greatsword at an angle.

[P133]
He was ready to attack. His troubled voice reached me.

[P134]
“Stop. I don’t want to do this either, but I have no choice.”

[P135]
I kept walking.

[P136]
“If you don’t want to, why are you here? Because you’re a hunting dog who can’t do anything but obey orders?”

[P137]
“……!”

[P138]
“If you’re afraid of Go Jun, say you’re afraid. Don’t dress it up as having no choice.”

[P139]
He wasn’t the only one. Everyone watching me had fear in their eyes.

[P140]
I continued forward. The more than a hundred people ahead of me backed away.

[P141]
The middle-aged man’s composure began to crack.

[P142]
“The tide has already turned. I heard Director Song returned to the United Kingdom this morning. What do you think that means? I had to find a way to survive. Even if it meant acting like a hunting dog.”

[P143]
Song Cheonwoo had gone to the United Kingdom this morning? Obviously a lie.

[P144]
Certain that Go Jun had sent a stand-in, I let out a quiet laugh.

[P145]
“What if that hunting dog’s master dies today?”

[P146]
“……!”

[P147]
Every eye widened.

[P148]
I reached into empty air and summoned White Flame from my Inventory. Its blade swept down diagonally.

[P149]
Swish!

[P150]
A single line cut through the air.

[P151]
Everyone caught their breath. But there was no spray of blood, no death.

[P152]
The Force that shot from the white spearhead had cut something other than a person.

[P153]
Slice. Crash!

[P154]
At the center of the garden stood an ornate fountain. The enormous stone statue planted atop it broke apart and collapsed.

[P155]
Fragments of a man already dead crushed the flowers below. Its severed head rolled across the ground until it came to rest at my feet.

[P156]
The statue was so lifelike I had no trouble recognizing its face.

[P157]
*Lee Jungryong.*

[P158]
That was right.

[P159]
Today, the magnificent palace built by an ambitious warlord who had wanted everything would fall.

[P160]
Along with the disciple who had become a monster.

[P161]
I tossed a few words at the stunned crowd.

[P162]
“You have two choices. Put down your weapons and clear a path, or cover my back.”

[P163]
“……!”

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
